case.title: The Boardwalk Fender Bender

memo.t: My cart was moving, then it stopped dead. So all of its energy just disappeared. Poof! Case closed, right?

stills.time: the front is built to crumple

case.question: Gus’s golf cart stopped dead. Did its energy really disappear? If not, where did it go?
case.how: Find 4 clues as you work through the lesson. Then crack the case (solve it) at the top of the Assignment tab.

clues.t: Your clapping hands stopped, but their energy didn’t vanish. It became the CLAP (sound) and warm palms (heat). Hard claps made more of both.

clues.where: The Lesson, Part 1: the energy coin bank
clues.t: In both crashes, every energy coin went somewhere: the other object’s motion, sound and heat. The Disappeared bin stayed empty.
In every bumper-car crash, BOTH cars changed how they moved. A car that slows or stops passes its motion to the other car.

clues.where: The Lesson, Part 4: the crash lab
clues.t: The heat camera showed warm spots where the balls hit. The squishier the crash, the more energy became heat and a dent.

solve.title: Where did the golf cart’s energy go?
solve.q: Which answer fits all four clues?

options.t: It disappeared, because the golf cart stopped.
options.why: Check Clue 2. Did any energy coin ever land in Disappeared?

options.t: Into Rosa’s cart (it rolled), the CRUNCH (sound), and heat in the dented bumpers.
options.why: Case cracked! The energy moved into motion, sound and heat. None of it disappeared. Strike! is open just below.

options.t: It all stayed inside the golf cart.
options.why: Check Clue 3. The golf cart stopped. A stopped cart doesn’t keep its motion.

options.t: Only into the sound of the crash.
options.why: Check Clue 4. What did the heat camera show where things hit?

clapper.afterText: What else could bump into it
clapper.title: The clap machine
todo: Pick a round: gentle claps or hard claps.
Clap as fast as you can for 5 seconds: press the 👏 button, tap the hands or press the space bar.
Do both rounds. Which made more sound and more heat?

why.t: Yes! Your two hands bump into each other. Every clap is a tiny collision.

clapper.alt: A model: two hands clapping, a sound meter that jumps with each clap, and a warm glow that grows on the palms.
clapper.pickMiss: Pick a round first: gentle or hard.

rounds.label: Gentle claps
rounds.line: Gentle claps! Your 5 seconds start with your first clap.

rounds.label: Hard claps
rounds.line: HARD claps! Your 5 seconds start with your first clap.

clapper.doneLine: Hard claps made more sound AND more heat. More energy went in, so more came out.
clapper.q: Your hands stopped moving after each clap. Where did their motion energy go?

opts.t: Into sound (the clap) and heat (warm palms).

opts.miss: Then why did your palms get warm, and what made the clap sound?

opts.t: Back into your arms, ready for the next clap.
opts.miss: Your arms make NEW motion for each clap. Where did the old motion go when the hands hit?

clapper.win: The clap was sound and the warm palms were heat. Clue 1!

bulletin.title: Rosa’s voicemail
todo: Press Play and listen. You can read along.
Tap the 3 clues that tell where the golf cart’s energy went.
lines: Hi Sam, it’s Rosa from the ice cream cart on the boardwalk.
Gus’s golf cart bumped my cart, and I heard a [[crunch|loud CRUNCH]]!
My whole cart [[roll|rolled about three feet]], and a scoop of mint chip fell off a cone.

When I touched the dent, the bumper felt [[warm|a little warm]]. [[x:That tells how Rosa felt, not where the energy went. Listen for something she heard, saw or felt with her hand.|I was so surprised!]] Call me back!
bulletin.win: Sound, motion and heat. Rosa just told Sam where the energy went!

coinbank.title: The energy coin bank
todo: Press Play the crash and watch.
Read the clue under each bin.
Drag every energy coin out of the bank to where the energy went (or tap a coin, then a bin). Tap a coin in a bin to send it back.
Then press Check my bank.

why.t: A pretend coin that stands for a share of the energy, so we can count where it goes. Real energy isn’t coins, but it can be counted with tools.

coinbank.playFirst: Play the crash first, so you can see where the energy went.
coinbank.bankLabel: BEFORE: the energy of the moving one (10 coins)
coinbank.leftMiss: Some coins are still in the bank. Every bit of energy went somewhere!

lost.miss: Energy never just disappears! Read the clues again. What did you hear? What got warm? What moved?

rounds.alt: A model: a bowling ball rolls into four pins. The pins fly up and away, and the ball keeps rolling slowly.

bins.ev: The pins flew across the lane.
The ball kept rolling, but slower.
The ball and pins got a tiny bit warmer where they hit.

rounds.someMiss: Look at the clue under “{bin}”: {ev} So some energy went there.
rounds.mostMiss: The pins flew the farthest. Give “{bin}” the most coins.
rounds.done: Close enough is great: nobody can count energy exactly by eye. What matters: 10 coins in, 10 coins out.

rounds.t: Golf cart and ice cream cart
rounds.alt: A model: a golf cart rolls into a parked ice cream cart. The golf cart stops, and the ice cream cart rolls away.

bins.ev: CRUNCH! The whole boardwalk heard it.
Both bumpers dented and felt warm.

rounds.zeroMiss: Look at the clue: Gus’s golf cart stopped dead. Can “{bin}” keep any coins?
rounds.someMiss: Look at the clue under “{bin}”: {ev} So some energy went there.
rounds.mostMiss: Which one moved the most after the crash? Give “{bin}” the most coins.
rounds.done: The golf cart kept zero coins, but none disappeared. They went into Rosa’s cart, the CRUNCH and the warm dents.

coinbank.q: What did the coin bank show about energy in a collision?

opts.t: Every bit of energy went somewhere: into motion, sound and heat.

opts.miss: Did the Disappeared bin ever keep a coin?

opts.t: All of it went into sound.
opts.miss: Look at your bins. Which got the most coins?

coinbank.win: 10 coins in, 10 coins out. Nothing disappeared. Clue 2!

bumpercars.afterText: BOTH objects change how they move
bumpercars.title: Bumper cars
todo: Set each car’s speed with − and +.
Predict who will change how it moves.
Press Crash! and read both speedometers. Do all 3 rounds.

why.t: A dial that shows how fast something is going, here in miles per hour (mph).

bumpercars.alt: A model: two bumper cars on a rink, a red one and a blue one.
bumpercars.predictQ: Predict: after the crash, who will change how it moves?
bumpercars.predMiss: Make a prediction first. Who will change how it moves?

rounds.sub: Round 1: the blue car is parked. The red car bumps it.
rounds.line: The mover passed most of its motion to the parked car.

rounds.sub: Round 2: both cars go the same way. The fast red car catches the slow blue car.
rounds.limitMiss: Keep the red car faster than the blue car, so it can catch up.
rounds.line: The fast car slowed down and the slow car sped up.

rounds.sub: Round 3: the cars drive toward each other.
rounds.line: Both slowed down, and at least one turned around.

bumpercars.q: In every bumper-car crash, who changed how it moved?

opts.t: Only the car that was hit.
opts.miss: Look at the red car’s speedometer before and after. Did it change?
Check the slower car’s speedometers too.

bumpercars.win: The mover doesn’t always win. Both cars changed every time. Clue 3!

crashlab.title: The crash lab
todo: Pick two balls: steel, rubber or clay.
Predict the AFTER, then press Crash them.
Switch on the heat camera. Where did it get warm? Do all three pairs.

why.t: A camera that sees warmth instead of light. Warm spots show up bright yellow and orange; cool things look dark blue.

crashlab.alt: A model: one ball rolls along a table toward a ball that is sitting still.
crashlab.pickMiss: Pick a pair of balls first.
crashlab.camFirst: Crash the balls first, then look with the heat camera.
crashlab.camNudge: Now switch on the heat camera.

preds.t: The moving ball stops, and the still ball rolls away
They stick together and roll slowly
The moving ball bounces straight back

pairs.after: Mover stopped; other rolled away fast
pairs.line: Steel balls bounce apart cleanly: almost all the motion passed to the other ball. The loud click took a little energy, and the heat camera shows only a tiny warm spot.

pairs.after: Mover almost stopped; other rolled a bit slower
pairs.line: Rubber squishes a little when it hits. More of the motion turned into heat, so the other ball rolled away a bit slower.
Clay squished flat and stuck. Lots of the motion turned into heat and a dent, so they rolled away slowly, together.

photo.head: The real thing: a heat camera at work
photo.alt: Two frames from a real heat-camera video. Left: a wooden stick rubs a wooden board, and the spot glows yellow and orange. Right: the stick is gone, but an orange warm mark stays on the board.
photo.cap: A real heat-camera video. Left: someone rubs a wooden stick hard on a wooden board, and the spot glows warm (yellow and orange). Right: the stick is gone, but the warm mark stays for a while. Rubbing and bumping both turn motion into heat.
photo.credit: Frames from “Heat by friction” by Laserlicht, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

crashlab.q: The clay balls slowed down the most. Where did their “missing” motion energy go?

opts.t: Into heat and squishing the clay (and a little sound).

opts.miss: Look at the heat camera. What glowed the brightest?
The table didn’t move. Where did the heat camera show a warm spot?

crashlab.win: The squishiest crash made the warmest spot. The “missing” energy became heat. Clue 4!

strike.kicker: Bonus game · unlocked after the case
strike.title: Strike!
todo: Drag the slider to aim. Pick a speed.
Roll! Every pin that falls passes energy to the pins behind it.
3 lanes, up to 9 stars.

why.q: Why do falling pins knock down other pins?
why.t: A falling pin is moving, so it carries energy. When it hits another pin, it passes some of that energy on: a chain of collisions.

strike.lockLine: Crack the case first. Then Strike! opens.
strike.alt: A model: a bowling lane seen from above, with the pins at the far end and the ball at the near end.

levels.name: Warm-up lane
levels.tip0: Knock down 7 or more pins for 2 stars. Every pin for 3!

levels.name: Pick up the spare
levels.tip0: Only 4 pins left, on the right. Aim carefully!

levels.name: Go for the strike
levels.tip0: Can you knock down all 10? You’ll need lots of energy and a perfect aim.

lines.none: Gutter! The ball missed the pins.
lines.aimTip: Aim closer to the front pin, so the falling pins knock the others.
lines.speedTip: Try a faster roll: more energy coins to pass along.

tool.name: Sound level meter
tool.teaser: Measure a whisper, a clap, a slammed door and more. Which collisions are loudest?
tool.done: You measured every sound. A sound level meter sticker is in your Field Notebook.

why.q: What does a sound level meter do?
why.t: It has a small microphone that measures how loud a sound is, in units called decibels (dB). A louder bang means more energy turned into sound.

soundmeter.title: How loud is that collision?
todo: Tap a sound to play it and measure it.
Watch the needle and read the decibels (dB).
Measure all 7. Your loudness ladder builds itself.
soundmeter.safeLine: Hearing experts say sounds of 85 dB or more can hurt your ears if you hear them for a long time.

sounds.note: Very little energy. It’s here so you can compare.
A tiny, gentle collision: a tiny bit of sound.
Normal talking, so you can compare.
Every bounce is a collision with the floor.
Your hands collide hard, and part of that energy becomes sound.
A heavy book hits the floor. Part of its energy becomes a BANG.
A big, fast collision: lots of energy turns into sound.

q.q: Which collisions turned the most energy into sound?

opts.t: The biggest, hardest bumps: the slammed door and the dropped book.
opts.why: Right! Harder collisions send more energy into sound, so the meter reads more decibels.
A whisper isn’t a collision, and it was the quietest of all.

opts.t: They all made the same amount of sound.
opts.why: Look at your ladder. Are all the bars the same length?

q1.A: A collision needs TWO things. What happens when two objects meet?
q1.C: Sunlight hitting a leaf moves light energy. A collision is two objects bumping.

q2.B: Remember the coin bank? Did any coin land in Disappeared?
q2.C: Energy can’t double. The coin bank always had 10 in and 10 out.

q3.A: A guess isn’t a prediction. What could you look at first?
q3.B: Waiting means it’s too late to predict! What can you see BEFORE the crash?

ans-3: Look at the crash test photo in the case file. Which part got crushed?

Think about the clap machine, the coin bank and the heat camera.

welcome.label: Welcome · the fender bender
welcome.script: Crunch! There was a crash on the boardwalk. Read the accident report and look at the drawing. Gus wrote that his cart’s energy just disappeared. Read his note. Can energy really vanish? Let’s find out where it went.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · the clap machine (Clue 1)
warmup.script: Your hands can collide too! Pick a round, gentle or hard. Then clap as fast as you can. Watch the sound meter jump, and watch the palms glow warmer. Which round made more sound and more heat?

vocab.label: Word Wall
vocab.notes: Clap once for “collision”; roll a ball into another for “motion change”.

part1.label: Part 1 · the energy coin bank (Clue 2)
part1.script: Press Play the crash and watch the ball hit the pins. Then drag every energy coin out of the bank, to where the energy went. Read the clue under each bin. Can a coin go in Disappeared? Try it!

part2.label: Part 2 · bumper cars (Clue 3)
part2.script: Bumper cars! Set each car’s speed with the minus and plus buttons. Predict who will change, then press Crash. Read both speedometers. Does the moving car always win?

explore.label: Part 4 · the crash lab (Clue 4)
explore.script: Welcome to the crash lab. Pick two balls: steel, rubber or clay. Predict the after, then crash them. Now switch on the heat camera. Where did it get warm?

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case
assignment.script: Do you have all four clues? Crack the case at the top of this tab, and a bowling game opens. Then answer two questions, fill in your before and after, and finish your C-E-R.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER
evidence.script: A classmate says all the energy disappears when two cars crash. Hmm. Think about your claps and the heat camera. Pick your side, tap two pieces of evidence, then explain how they prove your claim.

closing.label: Case closed
closing.script: Case closed! Gus’s energy never disappeared. It moved into Rosa’s cart, the crunch and the warm dent. Next time, you’ll run your own trials to test collision predictions.

hlCoach.title: Highlight like a scientist
tips: Highlight key words, not whole paragraphs.
If everything is yellow, nothing stands out. Aim for a few words in each paragraph.
Look for words that are explained.
Bold words, and words followed by “means”, “is called” or a meaning in ( ), are often worth saving.
Look for answers to the Big Question.
Ask yourself: does this help me explain what happens to energy when two objects bump?
“Because”, “so” and “first … then” show how ideas connect.
Yellow = important. Green = evidence I might use in my answer. Pink = something I wonder about.

practice.q: Practice: tap the 3 to 5 words that matter most in this sentence.
practice.text: In a collision, energy moves into motion, sound and heat, and none of it disappears.
practice.model: A scientist might highlight “collision”, “motion, sound and heat” and “none of it disappears”. Those words hold the big idea. Small words like “a” and “of” don’t carry the idea.

hlCoach.outside: This works in every subject. When you read anything, save the words that answer your question, and skip the rest.
